baselineFindings.finding: The reviews repository is localStorage-first and the review service declares provider local-mock, so browser state can create reviews and reputation outcomes.

Authenticated participants can insert directly into public.reviews and the policy requires status published, bypassing a server-owned command, moderation intake and idempotent acknowledgement boundary.

Browser eligibility requires completed order, released payment, linked charge and no active dispute, while remote RLS proves only completed-order participation and does not enforce payment release or dispute impact.
The database unique constraint protects order plus reviewer, but no server command idempotency, lost-response replay, concurrent submission or remote canary evidence is present.
New reviews are immediately published and no auditable moderation, report, sanction, restoration or appeal lifecycle is defined.
Professional reputation is aggregated in the browser from local reviews and is not a canonical server projection resistant to tampering, hidden rows, fraud or dispute reversals.
Review creation, order review flags, conversation mutation, charge mutation, notification and reputation events are separate browser writes without one atomic server transaction or durable outbox.
No canonical fraud controls, collusion detection, rate limits, text safety, personal-data redaction or suspicious-review hold rules are defined.
The remote policy permits either transaction participant to review the counterparty, while the active browser service supports only client-to-professional reviews; the product authority is ambiguous.
No canonical rehire command links repeat hiring to the prior completed order, current service snapshot, pricing, availability and a new Doke transaction.

mandatoryInvariants: authenticated UUID sessions never create authoritative reviews in localStorage
review submission uses a server-owned command and stable client request identity
only a participant of the exact completed order may review the configured counterparty
payment and dispute eligibility are evaluated by canonical server state
one review per configured actor and completed order is concurrency-safe
lost-response retries return the same review identity and outcome
new reviews enter an explicit moderation state rather than client-selected publication
review text is validated, rate-limited and protected against prohibited personal data
moderation, hiding, removal, restoration and appeal are append-only and audited
reputation is recalculated server-side from eligible canonical review revisions
hidden removed fraudulent or invalidated reviews cannot influence public reputation
dispute outcomes change reputation only through an approved versioned policy
review creation and transaction side effects are atomic or outbox-backed
public profile projections expose aggregate reputation without private risk signals
rehire creates a new Doke order linked to prior transaction history and current service authority
local fixtures and caches never create production reputation authority
